surprises.description: TNL reported adjusted EPS of $2.21, well above the preview's $2.05–$2.06 consensus and above its $2.15 bull-case threshold. The 23% year-over-year increase also exceeded the preview's 14% implied growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $2.05–$2.06” and “Implied YoY | +14%”; the bull case listed “$2.15+.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $1.1 billion, above the preview's $1.08 billion consensus, and grew 5% versus the 3.5% growth implied by consensus. This was a modest top-line beat.
Tours grew 7%, faster than the roughly 5% growth the preview said was needed and faster than Q2's 1%. This delivered stronger tour volume than the preview's operational baseline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Applying [the guide midpoint] requires ~210K tours, or ~+5% YoY”; tours had “decelerated sharply to +1% in Q2.”

surprises.description: VPG fell to $3,286, below the preview's $3,300–$3,350 company guide range, rather than remaining flat to slightly higher. Management attributed the decline to acquisition mix dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported volume per guest fell 1% to $3,286 due to acquisition mix dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “VPG | $3,300–$3,350”; the preview said this implied “essentially flat-to-+1.4% YoY.”

surprises.description: TNL raised and narrowed full-year guidance toward the top end instead of merely reaffirming the existing range: the EBITDA floor moved from $1.065 billion to $1.07 billion while the high end stayed at $1.085 billion. That is a positive change on the preview's main question about whether management would defend the demanding back-end-loaded outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised and narrowed full-year guidance to the top end,” including EBITDA of “$1.07B–$1.085B.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called FY26 EBITDA guidance of “$1,065–$1,085M” the “dominant variable” and said the market would watch whether it was “reaffirm[ed], raise[d], or trim[med].”

surprises.description: Travel and Membership revenue was $150 million, about $10 million below the preview's estimate of roughly $160 million; EBITDA was $51 million versus an estimate of about $52 million. The segment's decline therefore proved worse than the preview's already-weak outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The travel and membership segment posted $150 million revenue and $51 million EBITDA amid ongoing top-line decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “near $160M revenue and ~$52M EBITDA” if the decline persisted.

surprises.description: In response to the segment's ongoing decline, TNL announced a cost program affecting about 300 employees, expected to produce roughly $16 million in annualized savings, mostly in 2027. The preview discussed the segment's deterioration but did not anticipate this restructuring or quantified savings plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A cost program affecting ~300 employees [is] expected to deliver ~$16 million in annualized savings mostly in 2027.”

surprises.description: Management provided stronger evidence that the newer brands are scaling: Margaritaville Vacation Club is on pace for over $175 million in annual gross VOI sales, Accor Vacation Club is approaching $50 million in its third year, and new brands are expected to represent about 10% of sales this year. The preview did not quantify or flag this brand contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Margaritaville Vacation Club on pace for over $175 million in annual gross VOI sales,” “Accor Vacation Club approaching $50 million in only its third year,” and “new brands are expected to be ~10% of total sales mix this year.”

surprises.description: Management outlined a specific source of about $150 million of incremental liquidity in 2027—half from acquired receivables and half from retiring 17 lower-demand properties—and said it would support additional repurchases. This was more concrete and supportive of future buyback capacity than the preview's general expectation of early-2027 commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects ~$150 million of incremental liquidity in 2027 (half from acquired receivables, half from retiring 17 lower-demand properties), supporting additional share repurchase capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “capital return and early 2027 framing” and “any preliminary 2027 commentary,” but did not anticipate this liquidity amount or its sources.
